transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because I can’t get this thought out of my head… that after all my years working as an electrician, I still couldn’t keep my own brother safe. And if that’s true, then maybe I’m a danger to anybody working with me, or even anybody living under my roof.
Can you tell me more about what happened with your brother, and how long you’ve been feeling this way?
It started about four months ago. There was a garage fire, and after that my nephew came to live with us. Since then, I’ve been feeling this way pretty much constantly.
Since the fire, have you had any thoughts that keep coming back, even if you don’t want them, or felt like you need to do certain things over and over to feel safe or reduce your anxiety?

Yeah. It happens even when I’m trying to focus. I’ll be wiring a panel, or I’ll hear my nephew shut the garage door, and all of a sudden I’m right back there—smelling smoke, seeing my brother. It’s like the job site just drops out from under me for a minute.

Can you describe what happens when you have these experiences of being 'right back there'—do you feel as though you are actually reliving the fire or seeing it again in your mind, or does it feel more like a memory that just pops up?

It’s more than just a memory popping up. For a few seconds, it feels like I’m there again. I’ll be standing at a panel or hear that garage door shut, and suddenly I can smell smoke and see my brother. It’s like everything around me kind of drops away.
Since the fire, have you been feeling ongoing guilt or fear that you could have done something differently to prevent what happened to your brother?

Yeah. I keep thinking I should’ve done something different, like there had to be something I missed. And it’s not just guilt—it’s anger too. It just sits in my chest all day.

It gets worse when I look at my nephew. I think about how he lost his dad, and now he’s stuck with me instead. That part really messes with me.
Since the fire, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, people, or activities because they remind you of what happened?

Yeah. I avoid a lot of it now.

I don’t really go into my own garage unless I absolutely have to. I stopped helping with the electrical stuff at church, too. And if people start talking about car projects or bring up the fire, I shut it down pretty fast. I just can’t sit there and listen to it.
Since the fire, have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like your work, hobbies, or time with family?

I’m not sure. I mean, I still do the things I have to do. I haven’t really paid attention to whether it’s “interest” or just being tired of dealing with everything. Some days I don’t feel like doing much, but I don’t know if I’d say I’ve lost interest exactly.
Have you felt down, hopeless, or lost pleasure in things you used to enjoy, most of the day, nearly every day, since the fire?
I don’t really know. I’ve had rough days, yeah, but I haven’t been tracking it like that — “most of the day, nearly every day.” I can’t say for sure.
Since the fire, have you felt down or hopeless most days, even when there wasn’t a specific reminder of what happened?

Yeah… most days there’s this heavy feeling. It’s not always because something reminded me of the fire right then.

It’s more like guilt and anger just sitting in my chest. Especially when I look at my nephew and think… he lost his dad, and now he’s stuck with me instead. That thought hits me a lot.
Since the fire, have you found that you don’t get the same enjoyment out of things you used to like doing, like work, hobbies, or spending time with family?
I don’t know. I still go to work when I have to, and I’m around family, but I haven’t really thought about whether I enjoy it the same way. It’s more like I’m just getting through the day.
Since the fire, have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like your work, hobbies, or time with family?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do the things I’m supposed to do, but I haven’t stopped and thought, “Do I enjoy this?” It’s more like I’m just going through the motions.
Since the fire, have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things you used to enjoy, like your work, hobbies, or time with family?
I guess I can’t really say for sure. I haven’t been paying attention to whether I’m enjoying things or not. I still show up and do what I need to do, but I don’t really think about it beyond that.
Since the fire, have you noticed that you’ve lost interest in things you used to care about, like your work, hobbies, or spending time with family?

I’m not sure I’d call it lost interest. I still do the things I need to do, work and family stuff. I just haven’t really paid attention to whether I care about it the same way. It’s kind of hard for me to tell.
Since the fire, have you noticed that you’re not feeling good about things you used to look forward to, like work, hobbies, or time with family?
I’m not sure. I still do work and spend time with family when I’m supposed to. I just haven’t really noticed if I feel good about it or not. It’s more like I’m just getting through the day.
Since the fire, have you noticed that you’re less able to feel happiness or joy, even during things that used to make you happy, like spending time with family or finishing a good day’s work?
I don’t really know. I haven’t paid close enough attention to call it happiness or joy. I still do those things, like work and family stuff, but I’m mostly just going through the motions.
Since the fire, have you noticed that you’re less able to feel happiness or joy, even during things that used to make you happy, like spending time with family or finishing a good day’s work?

I don’t really know how to answer that. I can’t say I’ve noticed it clearly. I still do those things, but I don’t really stop and think, “Am I happy right now?” I’m just kind of getting through what I need to do.
